description: Work-package fragnet templates: the activities, logic (FS/SS/FF with lag), durations, materials and quality hold points the deterministic engine instances. This is the structure the admin fragnet editor exposes for editing (ADMIN_SPEC.md section 2). The LLM never emits these - it selects and reasons over them, and the engine instances them (CLAUDE.md rule 2).
provenance_summary: MIXED. The stage / owning department / key materials / key gates structure is transcribed from the DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md section 3 table. The ACTIVITY BREAKDOWNS, DURATIONS, LOGIC LINKS and LAGS are INDUSTRY ESTIMATES sized for a 20 MW-class Tier III build - typical sequences in the right range, not a record of how any project ran. A fragnet whose durations and logic are wrong produces a schedule that is internally consistent and completely wrong, which is harder to catch than an obvious error. This is a starter set establishing the shape; full discipline and commissioning depth is scheduled work, and the real depth should come from the client's historical schedules.

hold_points.name: PESO licence verified before HSD is received on site

provenance.note: Transformer-to-UPS installation and test. Switchgear and UPS install dominate; the sequence is gated by delivery, not by labour. Structure from docs/DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md#3; durations and logic are estimates. --- EXTENDED FOR REVIEW (three additions). c65 DIESEL GENERATOR SET INSTALLATION: lead.generator was in equipment_lead_times at 30 weeks with drives_rfs=true and was consumed by nothing, so the gensets never appeared in any programme and their lead time constrained nothing. It now carries a material link. Owner-furnished gensets (dp.ofe) change WHO procures, not the lead time, so the delivery gate applies either way. c67 BULK HSD STORAGE: the fuel system path.nm.peso_hsd licenses had no activity to gate; PESO is a safety approval for bulk diesel and its absence was a real hole. c70 HV/MV ENERGISATION: the package previously ended at cable termination, so there was no energisation step at all - which meant DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md#5 ("energisation cannot precede CEIG approval") had nothing to attach to, and safety.hv_energisation, a Tier-1 entry that BLOCKS EXPORT, matched no activity in any plan ever produced. THREE DURATIONS AND FIVE LOGIC LINKS ARE ESTIMATES. JUDGEMENTS TO CHALLENGE: 15 days for energisation assumes a single energisation event, where a 2N facility energises each path separately; the SS+10 from genset to fuel system assumes one contractor; and c65 hangs off c10 (plinth and pad preparation), which assumes the genset pads are poured with the transformer pads.

provenance.note: INVENTED FOR REVIEW. Stage, owning department (subcontract), materials (suppression, VESDA, BMS) and the two gates (fire NOC, NBC 2016) are transcribed from docs/DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md#3. The SIX ACTIVITIES, their SIX DURATIONS, the SEVEN LOGIC LINKS and the TWO HOLD POINTS are estimates: roughly 73 days on the longest path (detection -> BMS field -> head-end -> cause-and-effect). GROUNDED: the material link from the cylinder banks to lead.gas_suppression is real - the 16-week lead time in equipment_lead_times.json gates that activity, so suppression cannot start before the cylinders land. The safety_ref to safety.gas_suppression_discharge is also real and makes discharge testing a Tier-1 activity requiring sign-off. JUDGEMENTS TO CHALLENGE: cause-and-effect is modelled as one 15-day activity gating the fire NOC, where a real programme often runs it per-zone and re-tests; the three SS overlaps off detection assume one subcontractor sequencing gangs through the building rather than three independent trades. NOT MODELLED: the fire officer witnessing is a hold point, not a statutory pathway activity - the NOC itself lives in the city pathway data.

entries.name: Fit-out - containment, raised floor and structured cabling

activities.name: Raised floor and plinth installation to data halls
Horizontal cabling and patching to racks

hold_points.name: Raised floor level and load test

provenance.note: INVENTED FOR REVIEW. Stage, owning department, materials (containment, structured cabling) and the TIA-942 gate are transcribed from docs/DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md#3. The SIX ACTIVITIES, their SIX DURATIONS, the SIX LOGIC LINKS and the TWO HOLD POINTS are estimates sized for a 20-30 MW-class build: roughly 120 days on the longest path (raised floor -> containment -> backbone -> horizontal -> certification). JUDGEMENTS TO CHALLENGE: racks are placed after the raised floor and in parallel with the backbone, which assumes the floor carries the racks - a slab-mounted rack layout would reorder this; the SS+10 from floor to containment assumes containment follows the floor gang across the hall. NOT MODELLED: no material link to a long-lead item, because racks and cabling are not in equipment_lead_times.json - on a real project client-supplied racks are frequently the constraint here and their absence understates this stage. Also not modelled: fit-out is one whole-building package, so a hall-by-hall handover sequence is not represented. --- LOGIC REVISED FOR REVIEW: three finish-to-start links became start-to-start with a lead (f20->f30, f30->f50, f50->f60). Every activity in this package is per-hall except the backbone risers, so modelling them as one whole-building chain charged the programme for work that in reality runs concurrently across halls: horizontal cabling in the first hall does not wait for the backbone to reach the last one, and certification follows each hall rather than the building. THE THREE LEADS ARE ESTIMATES, set at roughly half the predecessor's duration, which is the crudest possible reading of 'about half the halls are ready'. They are the least defensible numbers in this entry and the first thing to replace with a per-zone sub-network.
provenance.warning: INDUSTRY ESTIMATE, NOT A PROJECT ACTUAL. A defensible typical figure for the Indian DC market, standing in until real execution data is loaded. No project ran to this number. Must be verified before use in a live plan.

hold_points.name: Snag list closure verified by the client

provenance.note: INVENTED FOR REVIEW. Stage, owning departments (PM, QA/QC) and the gates (occupancy certificate, warranties) are transcribed from docs/DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md#3. The SIX ACTIVITIES, their SIX DURATIONS, the SEVEN LOGIC LINKS and the TWO HOLD POINTS are estimates: about 85 days on the longest path (snagging -> TCCF -> final account). UPTIME TCCF (j30) IS AN ASSUMPTION ABOUT THIS PROJECT, not a universal step: Tier Certification of Constructed Facility is a demonstration to Uptime Institute after construction, and it applies only where the client is actually pursuing certification. A project building to Tier standards without certifying would delete j30 entirely. Its 20 days covers demonstration and report, not the certification cycle end to end. JUDGEMENTS TO CHALLENGE: TCCF is placed after snag closure and before final account, which assumes a single certification pass - a failed demonstration means remediation and a re-demonstration that this does not model. SCOPE DECISION: this package covers CONTRACTOR work only. The occupancy certificate and final fire NOC are statutory and deliberately absent, because the city pathway data already holds them with their own durations and blocking rules (path.nm.occupancy_certificate 8 weeks blocks handover; path.nm.fire_noc_final 10 weeks blocks occupancy). Duplicating them here would put two numbers for the same approval in two libraries, and CLAUDE.md rules that compliance is versioned data, not fragnet content. NOT MODELLED: the defects liability period itself, typically 12-24 months, which would dwarf the construction programme if drawn as an activity - j60 marks its commencement only.
